title: An Alabama animal shelter is taking on a massive AI data center project in court
excerpt: The Greater Birmingham Humane Society filed a lawsuit earlier this month in a bid to block Nebius Group's data center project in Alabama.
content_html:
By Natalie Musumeci

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

An Alabama animal shelter is barking back against a massive AI data center that's under construction next to its planned veterinary hospital campus in Birmingham.

The Greater Birmingham Humane Society filed a lawsuit earlier this month in a bid to block the project, alleging that the city of Birmingham, AL, and developers engaged in a "months-long scheme" to greenlight it by sidestepping zoning rules.

The lawsuit, filed in Jefferson County Circuit Court, says that the four-month review for building permits for the more than $2 billion facility moved at "lightning speed" compared with the 18-month review for the nonprofits' planned $67 million campus.

Entities of Nebius Group, the Amsterdam-headquartered AI infrastructure company behind the data center project, "coordinated" with the city to "abuse legal processes and manipulate timelines to fast-track a favored project without due process, regard for the law, or public welfare," the lawsuit alleges.

A Nebius spokesperson told Business Insider that the project was "permitted lawfully in this commercial district and Nebius has followed the same rules that apply to everyone else in Birmingham."

"The facility has also been thoughtfully designed and responsibly developed with measures including acoustical sound walls, grid power, and closed-loop cooling, among other areas," the spokesperson said.

A spokesperson for the city of Birmingham said the city does not comment on ongoing litigation.

The humane society's lawsuit says that the organization previously notified the city and its zoning board that the data center project "could deprive" it "of the planned use of its property because of noise that may interfere with its operations and be harmful to animals and humans."

The data center is being built about 160 feet from the property line of GBHS's future animal welfare campus, which is expected to include an adoption center, outdoor rehabilitation areas, and foster facilities, the nonprofit said.

"This case is not about whether data centers should exist," Allison Black Cornelius, the president and CEO of the GBHS, said in a statement. "It is about whether a project of this size and character should move forward in this location without the legal questions surrounding its approval first being resolved."

Cornelius added, "We believe neighboring institutions, nonprofit organizations, residents, and the broader community deserve confidence that the applicable laws and procedures have been followed."

Nebius' data center has also drawn separate legal action from area residents, according to local media reports.

The pushback comes amid growing community opposition to AI data center projects nationwide, driven by concerns about their environmental and economic impacts.

According to the research project Data Center Watch, at least 75 data center proposals worth an estimated $130 billion were delayed or blocked during the first three months of 2026 because of local opposition.

As of May, there were at least 430 local Facebook groups with more than 525,000 members fighting back against AI data centers, according to the Data Center Opposition Report, which tracks local opposition to the projects.

阿拉巴马州的一家动物收容所对正在伯明翰规划的兽医医院园区旁边正在建设的大型人工智能数据中心进行了反击。

大伯明翰人道协会本月早些时候提起诉讼，试图阻止该项目，声称阿拉巴马州伯明翰市和开发商参与了一项“长达数月的计划”，通过绕过分区规则来为该项目开绿灯。

该诉讼向杰斐逊县巡回法院提起，诉讼称，与该非营利组织计划耗资 6700 万美元的园区为期 18 个月的审查相比，这座价值超过 20 亿美元的设施的建筑许可证审查进度为“闪电般的速度”，为期四个月。

诉讼称，数据中心项目背后的总部位于阿姆斯特丹的人工智能基础设施公司 Nebius Group 的实体与该市“协调”，“滥用法律程序并操纵时间表，在没有正当程序、不尊重法律或公共福利的情况下快速推进受青睐的项目”。

Nebius 的一位发言人告诉《商业内幕》，该项目“在这个商业区得到了合法许可，并且 Nebius 遵循了适用于伯明翰其他所有人的相同规则。”

该发言人表示：“该设施还经过深思熟虑的设计和负责任的开发，采取了包括隔音墙、电网供电和闭环冷却等措施。”

伯明翰市发言人表示，该市不会对正在进行的诉讼发表评论。

人道协会的诉讼称，该组织此前通知市政府及其分区委员会，该数据中心项目“可能会剥夺”其财产的计划使用权，因为噪音可能会干扰其运营并对动物和人类造成伤害。

该非营利组织表示，该数据中心距离 GBHS 未来动物福利园区的地界线约 160 英尺，预计将包括一个收养中心、户外康复区和寄养设施。

GBHS 总裁兼首席执行官艾莉森·布莱克·科尼利厄斯 (Allison Black Cornelius) 在一份声明中表示：“此案与数据中心是否应该存在无关。” “问题在于，在不首先解决围绕其批准的法律问题的情况下，这种规模和性质的项目是否应该在这个地点推进。”

科尼利厄斯补充说：“我们相信邻近的机构、非营利组织、居民和更广泛的社区应该相信适用的法律和程序得到了遵守。”

据当地媒体报道，Nebius 的数据中心还引起了当地居民的单独法律诉讼。

出于对环境和经济影响的担忧，社区对全国人工智能数据中心项目的反对越来越多，而这一阻力正值此起彼伏。

根据研究项目“数据中心观察”的数据，由于当地的反对，2026 年前三个月至少有 75 个数据中心提案被推迟或阻止，价值估计为 1,300 亿美元。

根据跟踪当地对这些项目的反对情况的数据中心反对报告，截至 5 月，至少有 430 个当地 Facebook 群组，超过 525,000 名成员对人工智能数据中心进行反击。
